literal: Make plans again later."
idiomatic: and plan again when the moment comes."

literal: When Li Chong returned from campaign, Shen alone held military government.
idiomatic: When Li Chong returned, Shen alone held military authority.

literal: Pa-ling avoided the Rouran and moved south across the river.
idiomatic: Pa-ling evaded the Rouran and crossed the river south.

literal: Earlier separate general Li Shuren because Pa-ling pressed asked for relief; Shen went to him; before and after two hundred thousand surrendered.
idiomatic: General Li Shuren had begged relief when Pa-ling pressed him; Shen marched to him and two hundred thousand surrendered.

literal: Shen with the Mobile Office Yuan Zuan memorialized asking north of Heng to separately establish commanderies and counties to settle the surrendered households, according to need to relieve and grant, quieting their rebellious hearts.
idiomatic: Shen and Yuan Zuan of the mobile office asked to settle the surrendered north of Heng in new counties, feeding them to quiet rebellion.

literal: Not followed.
idiomatic: The court refused.

literal: An edict sent Yellow Gate Attendant Yang to disperse them among Ji, Ding, and Ying three provinces for food.
idiomatic: An edict sent Yang to scatter them among Ji, Ding, and Ying for grain.

literal: Shen said to Zuan: "These people again become beggars for life.
idiomatic: Shen told Zuan, "You have made beggars of them again.

literal: Disaster and disorder will arise from this."
idiomatic: Disaster will follow."

literal: Soon Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Dingzhou, Du Luozhou at Youzhou; the rest of the surrendered still at Heng then wished to make Shen their leader.
idiomatic: Soon Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Ding, Du Luozhou at You; the remaining surrendered at Heng tried to make Shen their chief.

literal: Shen then submitted a memorial begging return to the capital.
idiomatic: Shen memorialized begging to return to the capital.

literal: Ordered Left Guards General Yang Jin to replace Shen as commander; Shen made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Right Guards General, Inspector of Ding.
idiomatic: Left guards general Yang Jin replaced him; Shen became attendant-in-ordinary, right guards general, and inspector of Ding.

literal: At that time Zhongshan Administrator Zhao Shulong and Vice Director Cui Rong attacking bandits failed; the office envoy Liu Shen was examining and not finished when bandits pressed Zhongshan; Shen then ordered Shulong to guard the border.
idiomatic: When Zhao Shulong and Cui Rong failed against rebels and inspector Liu Shen had not finished his review, bandits pressed Zhongshan; Shen ordered Shulong to hold the line.

literal: Shen galloped post-horses back to the capital, saying Shen on his own authority had been lax.
idiomatic: Liu Shen raced to the capital accusing Guangyang Shen of lax command.

literal: Prince of Chengyang Hui and Shen had a rift; therefore he framed him.
idiomatic: Prince Hui of Chengyang hated Shen and framed him.

literal: Then summoned Shen as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrent Commander of the Central Army.
idiomatic: Shen was recalled as director of personnel and central army commander.

literal: When Shen reached the capital Emperor Ming did not wish Hui and Shen to resent each other; he ordered at a banquet that they reconcile.
idiomatic: At the capital Emperor Ming ordered a banquet to reconcile Shen and Hui.

literal: Hui harbored resentment without end.
idiomatic: Hui's grudge never ended.

literal: Later Prince of Hejian Chen and others were defeated by Xianyu Xiuli; then Shen was made equal thirds with the Three Excellencies and Grand Commander.
idiomatic: When Prince Chen of Hejian fell to Xianyu Xiuli, Shen was made grand commander with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: Prince of Zhangwu Rong was left commander, Pei Yan right commander, both receiving Shen's direction.
idiomatic: Prince Rong of Zhangwu commanded the left, Pei Yan the right, both under Shen.

literal: Hui therefore memorialized to Empress Dowager Ling framing Shen saying: "Guangyang holds his beloved son with troops outside—he cannot be measured."
idiomatic: Hui told Empress Ling, "Guangyang keeps his beloved son in command abroad—who can trust him?"

literal: Then ordered Prince of Zhangwu and others secretly to guard against one another.
idiomatic: She secretly ordered Rong and the others to watch him.

literal: Rong then showed the edict to Shen.
idiomatic: Rong showed Shen the edict.

literal: Shen feared; on matters large and small he dared not decide himself.
idiomatic: Shen grew afraid and dared decide nothing alone.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling hearing this sent to ask Shen's true intent; he then fully stated saying:
idiomatic: The empress dowager asked his mind; he answered at length:

literal: Formerly when Yuan Cha held power he moved heaven and shifted the sun, yet Hui clung to him and flew without wings.
idiomatic: "When Yuan Cha moved heaven and earth, Hui clung to him and rose without wings.

literal: Now the great brightness has returned to government; trust and commission are only weighty; because Hui's heart is narrow he hates your servant to the bone.
idiomatic: Now the throne is restored, yet Hui's narrow heart hates me to the bone.

literal: Your servant because coarse and stagnant was far from the capital carriage, framed and obstructed by him—there was nothing he did not do.
idiomatic: Far from court, I was framed at every turn.

literal: Yet your servant was not formerly behind him; from then until now it has turned into deep valley.
idiomatic: I was never his follower; since then he has buried me.

literal: Hui then eight promotions in one year, position reaching chancellor;
idiomatic: Hui was promoted eight times in a year to chancellor;

literal: your servant was stalled many years, merit unrecorded.
idiomatic: I stagnated for years while merit went unrecorded.

literal: From when Hui held government, not only was your servant suppressed—northern expedition merits were all blocked.
idiomatic: Since he took power he has blocked not only me but every northern merit.

literal: Officers and soldiers reporting victory in the end had not a shred of reward;
idiomatic: Soldiers who won received nothing;

literal: though memorialized, many were not granted.
idiomatic: memorials for reward were refused.

literal: Earlier Yuan Biao was left at Shengle, later besieged in heavy rings; splitting bones they traded sons, hung upside down in a corner.
idiomatic: Yuan Biao held Shengle until besieged; men ate their children; the city hung by a thread.

literal: Besieged two years; after the bandits scattered, according to rank he begged office; Hui then turned back and did not grant what was asked.
idiomatic: After two years he begged office by rank; Hui refused.

literal: Yet Xuzhou Xiapi garrison commander Jia Xun, after Faseng's rebellion was for a time besieged—the merit of firm defense compared with that was not heavier—yet he at once received a province and was enfeoffed a state founder.
idiomatic: Jia Xun held Xiapi through Faseng's siege with lesser merit yet won a province and a founding marquisate.

literal: Affairs under heaven flow one way—equal merit yet different reward; what is imbalance called!
idiomatic: Merit is equal, reward unequal—what justice is that?

literal: Also when Cavalry General Li Chong on the northern expedition opened recruitment of men from eight provinces, hearing use of the Guanxi scale.
idiomatic: When Li Chong marched north he promised Guanxi pay to recruits from eight provinces.

literal: When your servant was behind, according to this rule he rewarded.
idiomatic: Behind him I paid by that scale.

literal: Again saying northern-route campaigners could not be the same as Guanxi.
idiomatic: Hui then said northern troops must not match Guanxi.

literal: Dingxiang tomb-shrine is of the utmost weight, Pingcheng guarding the state's vital fortress—if counting this to discuss merit, how is it inferior to Qin and Chu?
idiomatic: Dingxiang's tombs and Pingcheng's walls weigh as heavy as Qin and Chu—how are their defenders less deserving?

literal: Only because of hatred of your servant he then wished to suppress on sight of wind.
idiomatic: He suppresses them only because they follow me.

literal: Yet from when he held the road until now, how is it only retreating merit!
idiomatic: His spite does not stop at denying merit.

literal: Whoever followed your servant on campaign at once became what he envied.
idiomatic: Anyone who marched with me becomes his enemy.

literal: Commander Yuan Shuhe once appealed to the ministry; Hui at first said there was reason, then hearing northern expedition was subordinate to your servant as commander, at once changed color.
idiomatic: Commander Yuan Shuhe appealed; Hui first agreed, then turned hostile when he learned Shuhe served under me.

literal: Again ordering your servant's brother's son Zhongxian to sue your servant with strange pleas, weaving and fluttering, plotting mutual slander.
idiomatic: He set my nephew Zhongxian to sue me with endless slander.

literal: Those who spoke your servant's evil he met with favoring countenance;
idiomatic: He smiles on those who call me wicked;

literal: those who called your servant good at once were suspected and reproached.
idiomatic: he punishes those who praise me.

literal: Zhen Chen once judged your servant's wrong and then looked on him as enemy;
idiomatic: Zhen Chen once judged my case fairly and became his foe;

literal: Xu He often spoke your servant's faults yet was treated like a kinsman.
idiomatic: Xu He spoke my faults yet is treated like kin.

literal: Also Cavalry General Chief Clerk Zu Ying, formerly in the army falsely added head-count;
idiomatic: Zu Ying, chief clerk to the cavalry general, once inflated head counts in camp;

literal: distorting the army's march, harming the military office, guilty before the law, avoiding fate in mountains and marshes.
idiomatic: he corrupted the army, fled justice to the hills,

literal: Only because of slandering your servant Hui then returned and cleared his crime.
idiomatic: yet Hui cleared him because he slandered me.

literal: Your servant's office Marshal Liu Jing, comparing in escorting surrendered men, when they reached Dingzhou turned and rebelled; bandits like a bursting river—how could he embrace them?
idiomatic: My marshal Liu Jing escorted surrendered men who rebelled at Ding like a bursting river—how could he hold them?

literal: And because he was your servant's office staff, he did not escape body and head in different places.
idiomatic: Because he served my office, he died dismembered.

literal: Hui being angry and transferred, he let go the chief evil and grasped the clerks.
idiomatic: Hui punished clerks and spared the chief culprit.

literal: Those who followed your servant—none failed to tremble in fear.
idiomatic: All who followed me tremble.

literal: Recently the people of Heng begged your servant as inspector; Hui then spoke fluently that it could not be measured.
idiomatic: When Heng begged me as inspector, Hui called me unpredictable.

literal: When the surrendered plotted, your servant repeatedly memorialized; Hui then seized on this matter.
idiomatic: When the surrendered plotted, I reported it; he seized the tale.

literal: And when going to Dingzhou, far from those wicked men, again he spoke that your servant would have a different intent.
idiomatic: As I went to Ding he again said I meant treason.

literal: Turning over like this, wishing to trap and destroy.
idiomatic: He twists every way to destroy me.

literal: Causing the dynastic court hastily to grant transfer and replacement.
idiomatic: The court hurried my recall.

literal: The origin of the bandits' rise—who made it so?
idiomatic: Who made the rebels rise?

literal: Hui being favored and privileged, his commission lofty for a generation—those who admired power, what did they have toward your servant!
idiomatic: Hui is favored for a generation; who courts power visits him, not me.

literal: Therefore others when holding selection, carriages and horses filled the gate.
idiomatic: When others held appointments, their gates choked with carriages.

literal: When your servant dwelt on the frontier, guests and travelers rarely came.
idiomatic: On the frontier my gate was empty.

literal: Your servant recently feared he would be an obstruction, therefore diligently begged to go to the capital.
idiomatic: I begged the capital fearing he would block me.

literal: Just when exiles raised axes and the grand commander drooped wings, again following the later order, self at ease nowhere;
idiomatic: When exiles took up axes and armies folded, I obeyed again with nowhere to rest;

literal: bowing head as vanguard, not daring to decline affairs.
idiomatic: I bowed and marched ahead, not daring refuse.

literal: When your servant left the capital the marching dust was not yet settled when already heard behind of fresh different discussion.
idiomatic: I had barely left the capital when fresh slander followed.

literal: Saying your servant would have his son follow himself, proof of a suspicious omen.
idiomatic: He said I brought my son as proof of treason.

literal: Suddenly using this to frame disorder.
idiomatic: He used that to cry rebellion.

literal: Loose people again transmitted sounds, saying left army your servant Rong, right army your servant Yan both received secret edicts to watch your servant's affairs.
idiomatic: Rumors said Rong on the left and Yan on the right held secret orders to spy on me.

literal: Hui having used his heart thus, how can your servant secure himself?
idiomatic: With Hui's heart thus, how can I be safe?

literal: I venture that the heavenly step is not yet level, national difficulty still blocks;
idiomatic: The realm is not yet at peace; calamity still blocks the way.

literal: the duty of regional lords is at this time urgent.
idiomatic: Provincial command is urgent now.

literal: Hui formerly on the frontier had men's praise; dwelling at the summit right, none heard of it.
idiomatic: Hui was praised on the frontier; at court center he is unheard of.

literal: Now beg to send him out as a province, let him declare his useful service.
idiomatic: Send him out to a province where he may prove useful.

literal: If Hui outside follows his strength, your servant has no inner worry's cut.
idiomatic: If he serves abroad by his talent, I need not fear him within.

literal: If I receive this, public and private are greatly fortunate.
idiomatic: Grant this and public and private alike will prosper."

literal: Shen because the soldiers had repeatedly retreated and scattered, men had no fighting heart; linking camps and turning palisades, each day marched ten li.
idiomatic: Shen's men had retreated so often they would not fight; he chained camps and crept ten li a day.

literal: March reaching Jiaojin, across water they formed battle lines.
idiomatic: At Jiaojin he drew up across the water.

literal: Bandit Xiuli often plotted with Ge Rong; later he slightly trusted Shuozhou man Mao Puxian; Rong often resented this.
idiomatic: Xiuli often plotted with Ge Rong but later trusted Mao Puxian of Shuozhou, whom Rong resented.

literal: Puxian formerly was Shen's commander; when at Jiaojin, Shen sent word urging him; Puxian then had intent to surrender.
idiomatic: Puxian had served under Shen; at Jiaojin Shen urged him and he wavered toward surrender.

literal: Also sent Recorder-Adjutant Yuan Yan to persuade bandit Cheng Shagui.
idiomatic: He sent Yuan Yan to sway the bandit Cheng Shagui.

literal: Indeed they mutually suspected and divided.
idiomatic: Suspicion split the rebels.

literal: Ge Rong then killed Puxian and Xiuli and established himself.
idiomatic: Ge Rong killed Puxian and Xiuli and took command.

literal: Rong because he newly had a great multitude, above and below not yet at peace, then went north crossing Ying Province.
idiomatic: Rong, uneasy with his new horde, marched north into Ying.

literal: Shen then led the multitude turning north.
idiomatic: Shen turned north after him.

literal: Rong east attacked Prince of Zhangwu Rong; Rong was defeated at White Ox Return.
idiomatic: Rong struck Prince Rong of Zhangwu and broke him at White Ox Return.

literal: Shen then retreated running, hurrying to Dingzhou.
idiomatic: Shen fled toward Ding.

literal: Hearing Inspector Yang Jin suspected he had a different intent, he then stopped at a Buddhist temple south of the province.
idiomatic: Hearing that Inspector Yang Jin suspected treason, he halted at a temple south of the city.

literal: Stopped two days and nights, then summoned Commanders Mao Mi and six or seven others, arms on shoulders as covenant, in peril's moment expecting to save and comfort one another.
idiomatic: After two nights he arm-linked Mao Mi and six officers, swearing to save one another in peril.

literal: Mi suspected Shen's intent was different and secretly reported to Jin, saying Shen plotted not to follow the law.
idiomatic: Mi doubted him and told Jin that Shen plotted rebellion.

literal: Jin sent Mi to attack Shen.
idiomatic: Jin sent Mi against him.

literal: Shen ran out; Mi shouted and chased close.
idiomatic: Shen fled; Mi shouted and pursued.

literal: Shen with attendants reaching Boling commandery border met bandit roaming horsemen, then led to Ge Rong.
idiomatic: At Boling he met rebel scouts and was brought to Ge Rong.

literal: Bandit followers seeing Shen were somewhat pleased.
idiomatic: Many rebels rejoiced to see him.

literal: Rong newly established himself, inwardly hated him, then harmed Shen.
idiomatic: Rong, newly risen, hated him inwardly and killed him.
